54.example: Fig. 2 shows a Mughal army on campaign.

54.english_meaning: Large, heavy guns formerly used in warfare, typically mounted on wheels.
54.hindi_meaning: तोपें (युद्ध में उपयोग किए जाने वाले बड़े और भारी हथियार)
54.example: Cannons were an important addition in sixteenth-century warfare.

54.english_meaning: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.
54.hindi_meaning: वंशज (किसी पूर्वज की संतान या आने वाली पीढ़ियाँ)
54.example: The Mughals were descendants of two great lineages of rulers.

54.english_meaning: A lineal descent from an ancestor; ancestry or pedigree.
54.hindi_meaning: वंश / कुल (किसी पूर्वज से चली आ रही पारिवारिक परंपरा या वंश)
54.example: They were descendants of two great lineages of rulers.

54.english_meaning: A person or thing that succeeds another, especially in holding an office, title, or throne.
54.hindi_meaning: उत्तराधिकारी (गद्दी, पद या अधिकार को संभालने वाला अगला व्यक्ति)
54.example: From their father's side, they were the successors of Timur.

54.english_meaning: An indiscriminate and brutal slaughter of many people.
54.hindi_meaning: नरसंहार / कत्लेआम (बड़ी संख्या में लोगों की क्रूरतापूर्ण हत्या)
54.example: Genghis Khan’s memory was associated with the massacre of innumerable people.

54.english_meaning: Too many to be counted; countless.
54.hindi_meaning: अगणित / अनगिनत (इतने अधिक जिनकी गिनती न की जा सके)
54.example: His memory was linked with the massacre of innumerable people.

54.english_meaning: A person, team, or company who is competing against others.
54.hindi_meaning: प्रतिस्पर्धी / प्रतिद्वंदी (आपसी मुकाबले में खड़े लोग या समूह)
54.example: The Uzbegs were their Mongol competitors.

54.english_meaning: One's family or ethnic descent; forebears.
54.example: The Mughals were proud of their Timurid ancestry.

54.english_meaning: A line of descent traced continuously from an ancestor.
54.hindi_meaning: वंशावली (पूर्वजों की पूरी सूची या पारिवारिक इतिहास)

54.english_meaning: In a way that relates to or is expressed in pictures.
54.hindi_meaning: चित्रों के माध्यम से / चित्रात्मक रूप से
54.example: They celebrated their genealogy pictorially, getting pictures made.

54.english_meaning: Inherited from or belonging to one's forebears or ancestors.
54.example: He was forced to leave his ancestral throne.

54.english_meaning: An instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.
54.hindi_meaning: आक्रमण / हमला (सैनिक बल द्वारा किसी क्षेत्र पर कब्जा करने की कार्रवाई)
54.example: He lost his throne due to the invasion of another Mongol group.

54.english_meaning: Moving aimlessly from place to place.
54.example: After years of wandering, he seized Kabul.

54.english_meaning: Took hold of something suddenly and forcibly.
Connected with something else in someone's mind.
54.example: Genghis Khan’s memory was associated with the massacre of innumerable people.

54.english_meaning: Took into possession or control, especially by force.
54.example: Their great ancestor had captured Delhi and Agra.

55.english_meaning: The state of being the firstborn child, and the right of the eldest son to inherit his father's entire estate.
55.hindi_meaning: ज्येष्ठ अधिकार (वह प्रथा जिसमें सबसे बड़े पुत्र को पिता की सारी संपत्ति मिलती है)
55.example: The Mughals did not believe in the rule of primogeniture.

55.english_meaning: Received money, property, or a title as an heir upon the death of the previous holder.
55.hindi_meaning: विरासत में पाना या उत्तराधिकार में प्राप्त करना
55.example: The eldest son inherited his father’s estate under the system.

55.english_meaning: All the money and property owned by a particular person, especially at death.
55.example: He managed the large estate left behind by his ancestors.

55.english_meaning: A traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a particular society, place, or time.
55.example: They followed the ancient custom of sharing property.

55.english_meaning: A system of joint heirship where an estate is divided equally among all the sons or heirs.
55.hindi_meaning: सह-दायभाग (संपत्ति का सभी पुत्रों के बीच समान रूप से विभाजन)
55.example: The Mughals followed the Timurid custom of coparcenary inheritance.

55.english_meaning: The action of separating something into parts or the process of being separated.
55.example: The division of property caused disputes among the family.

55.english_meaning: Just, unbiased, and equitable; treating everyone equally according to the rules.
55.example: Which do you think is a fairer division of inheritance?

55.english_meaning: Series of military operations intended to achieve a particular objective, typically during a war.
55.example: The Mughal rulers campaigned constantly against rival kings.

55.english_meaning: Continuously over a period of time; repeatedly.
55.example: The empire was constantly expanding its borders.

55.english_meaning: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
55.example: Many rulers refused to accept the authority of the emperor.

55.english_meaning: Done, given, or acting of one's own free will without being forced.
55.hindi_meaning: स्वेच्छा से या अपनी मर्जी से
55.example: Many regional rulers joined the alliance voluntarily.
They received high positions in the imperial court.

55.english_meaning: A rank or status in an organization, society, or government.
55.example: Loyal nobles were appointed to important administrative positions.

55.english_meaning: Stood firm against or fought against someone or something.
55.example: The local chieftains resisted the foreign invasion fiercely.

55.english_meaning: The daughter of a monarch or ruler.
55.example: The Rajput princess was married to the Mughal prince.

55.english_meaning: Relating to the present time; contemporary.
55.example: Amber is located in modern-day Jaipur.

55.english_meaning: Relating to the armed forces or to soldiers, warfare, and defense.
55.example: The military strength of the kingdom grew rapidly under his rule.

55.english_meaning: Controlled, managed, or governed by someone or something.
55.hindi_meaning: के अधीन या के नेतृत्व में
55.example: Many reforms were introduced under Akbar.

56.english_meaning: A numerical rank in the Mughal mansabdari system that determined a noble's position, status, and salary in court.
56.hindi_meaning: जात (मुग़ल प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था में मनसबदार का पद, प्रतिष्ठा और वेतन निर्धारित करने वाला एक संख्यात्मक दर्जा या रैंक।)
56.example: Nobles with a zat of 5,000 were ranked higher than those of 1,000 in the royal court.

56.english_meaning: An official or noble in the Mughal administration holding a rank or position.
56.hindi_meaning: मनसबदार (मुग़ल काल में वह अधिकारी या जागीरदार जिसे कोई विशेष 'मनसब' या पद सौंपा गया हो।)
56.example: By Aurangzeb’s reign, the number of mansabdars had significantly increased.

56.english_meaning: A holder of a jagir, who was assigned land revenue in lieu of a cash salary.
56.hindi_meaning: जागीरदार (वह व्यक्ति जिसे वेतन के बदले राजस्व वसूलने के लिए भूमि का क्षेत्र यानी जागीर सौंपी जाती थी।)
56.example: Unlike earlier systems, most jagirdars did not actually reside in or administer their assigned territories.

56.english_meaning: The action of spending funds or money by a government, organization, or person.
56.hindi_meaning: व्यय / खर्च (सरकार या किसी संस्था द्वारा धन खर्च करने की प्रक्रिया।)
56.example: An increase in the number of high-ranking nobles would have meant more expenditure for the state.

56.english_meaning: A task, duty, or specific tract of land given to someone as a duty.
56.hindi_meaning: सौंपी गई भूमि या कार्य / जागीर (किसी व्यक्ति को प्रशासनिक कार्य या राजस्व के लिए आवंटित क्षेत्र।)
56.example: They were given their lands back as assignments after being defeated and honourably treated.

56.english_meaning: Causing a loss of pride or self-respect; deeply embarrassing.
56.hindi_meaning: अपमानजनक (किसी का आत्मसम्मान ठेस पहुँचाने वाला या नीचा दिखाने वाला।)
56.example: The careful balance between defeating but not humiliating their opponents enabled the Mughals to extend their authority.

56.hindi_meaning: शामिल करना / घेर लेना (विस्तृत क्षेत्र या विभिन्न समूहों को अपने दायरे में समेटना।)
56.example: As the empire expanded to encompass different regions, the Mughals recruited diverse bodies of people.

56.english_meaning: To enlist someone in the armed forces or service.
56.hindi_meaning: भर्ती करना (सेवा या सेना में नए लोगों को शामिल करना।)
56.example: The Mughals recruited diverse groups of people into their administrative service.

56.english_meaning: A central group of people or things around which others are collected.
56.hindi_meaning: केंद्रीय केंद्र / मूल समूह (वह छोटा प्रारंभिक समूह जिसके इर्द-गिर्द कोई संस्था या व्यवस्था विकसित होती है।)
56.example: From a small nucleus of Turkish nobles, the administration expanded to include many other groups.

56.english_meaning: Inspiring respect and admiration; having high status.
56.hindi_meaning: प्रतिष्ठित / सम्मानजनक (उच्च सम्मान या ख्याति प्राप्त।)
56.example: The higher the zat, the more prestigious was the noble’s position in court.

56.english_meaning: A soldier who fights on horseback.
56.hindi_meaning: घुड़सवार सैनिक (घोड़े पर सवार होकर युद्ध करने वाला सैनिक।)
56.example: The mansabdar was required to maintain a specified number of cavalrymen.

56.english_meaning: Marked with a brand for identification, especially horses in military reviews.
56.hindi_meaning: दागा हुआ / मुहरबंद (पहचान के लिए घोड़ों पर गर्म लोहे से निशान या दाग लगाना।)
56.example: The mansabdar brought his cavalrymen for review, got them registered, and their horses branded.

56.english_meaning: Income that a government or state collects from land, taxes, or other sources.
56.hindi_meaning: राजस्व (सरकार या राज्य को कर या भूमि से प्राप्त होने वाली आय।)
56.example: Jagirdars received their salaries as revenue assignments called jagirs.

56.english_meaning: To manage and organize the running of a region, institution, or system.
56.hindi_meaning: प्रशासन चलाना / प्रबंध करना (किसी क्षेत्र या व्यवस्था की देखरेख और संचालन करना।)
56.example: Most jagirdars did not actually reside in or administer their assigned land territories.

56.english_meaning: To have one's permanent home in a particular place.
56.hindi_meaning: निवास करना / रहना (किसी स्थान पर स्थायी रूप से रहना।)
56.example: Unlike local rulers, the jagirdars did not reside in the provinces they collected revenue from.

56.english_meaning: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
56.hindi_meaning: सत्ता / अधिकार (शासन चलाने या निर्णय लेने की शक्ति।)
56.example: The Mughals successfully established their authority over different regions of India.

56.english_meaning: Officially registered as a member of an institution or service.
56.hindi_meaning: नामांकित / भर्ती किया गया (किसी सेवा या सूची में आधिकारिक रूप से दर्ज होना।)
56.example: Those who joined Mughal service were enrolled as mansabdars.

56.english_meaning: Relating to or expressed as a number or numbers.
56.hindi_meaning: संख्यात्मक (संख्याओं से संबंधित या संख्याओं में व्यक्त किया गया।)
56.example: The rank and salary of a mansabdar were determined by a numerical value called zat.

57.english_meaning: The period during which a sovereign rules.
57.example: In Akbar’s reign, revenues were carefully assessed.

57.english_meaning: Income that a government receives from taxes and other sources.
57.example: The main source of income available to Mughal rulers was tax revenue.

57.english_meaning: An official in the Mughal administration holding a rank or mansab.
57.example: A mansabdar on march with his sawars.

57.english_meaning: The class of farmers who own or rent small pieces of land for cultivation.
57.example: The peasantry suffered tremendously during the later years of Aurangzeb's reign.

57.english_meaning: A landholder or intermediary who collected taxes from peasants in Mughal India.
57.example: The Mughals used one term – zamindars – to describe all intermediaries.

57.english_meaning: A person who acts as a link between people, such as a broker or tax collector.
57.example: Zamindars acted as intermediaries between the state and the peasants.

57.english_meaning: The leader of a people, clan, or local district.
57.example: Peasants paid taxes through local headmen or powerful chieftains.

57.english_meaning: An investigation or study of an area, land, or data.
57.example: Todar Mal carried out a careful survey of crop yields and prices.

57.english_meaning: To prepare and use land for growing crops.
57.example: The survey recorded the areas cultivated over a 10-year period.

57.english_meaning: The Mughal land revenue system based on crop yields and fixed rates.
57.example: This revenue system was known as zabt.

57.english_meaning: Widespread in a particular area at a particular time.
57.example: This system was prevalent in areas where administrators could survey the land.

57.english_meaning: A person responsible for running a business, organization, or government system.
57.example: Mughal administrators maintained very careful land accounts.

57.english_meaning: A principal administrative division of a country or empire.
57.example: Land surveys were not possible in provinces such as Gujarat and Bengal.

57.english_meaning: A very small painting or work of art, common in historical manuscripts.
57.example: Details from a miniature depicted corruption in the administration.

57.english_meaning: Dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power, typically involving bribery.
57.example: The painting depicted corruption in the administration.

57.english_meaning: A sum of money or favor offered to someone to influence their behavior dishonestly.
57.example: The official was caught receiving a bribe from a merchant.

57.english_meaning: A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained in sufficient amounts.
57.example: These factors created a shortage in the number of assignments available.

57.english_meaning: To obtain something from someone, often by force, pressure, or persuasion.
57.example: Many tried to extract as much revenue as possible.

58.english_meaning: A landowner or agrarian intermediary in Mughal India who collected revenue from peasants.
58.hindi_meaning: ज़मींदार (भारत के इतिहास में वह व्यक्ति जो किसानों से भू-राजस्व एकत्र करता था)
58.example: In some rural areas, the zamindars exercised a great deal of economic and social power.

58.english_meaning: The action or fact of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work.
58.hindi_meaning: शोषण (किसी व्यक्ति या वर्ग का अपने लाभ के लिए अनुचित उपयोग या अत्याचार)
58.example: The exploitation by Mughal administrators forced the peasants to rebel.

58.english_meaning: An attempt to put down the authority of a ruler or government; a rebellion.
58.hindi_meaning: विद्रोह (सत्ता या सरकार के खिलाफ बगावत)
58.example: These peasant revolts challenged the stability of the Mughal Empire.

58.english_meaning: The state of being stable, secure, and unlikely to change or fall.
58.example: Internal conflicts and frequent uprisings threatened the stability of the kingdom.

58.english_meaning: A sovereign head of state, especially a king, queen, or emperor.
58.example: Nur Jahan remained extremely loyal and supportive to the Mughal monarch, Jahangir.

58.english_meaning: Words inscribed or engraved on a coin, monument, or piece of metal.
58.hindi_meaning: उत्कीर्ण लेख / अभिलेख (सिक्के या पत्थर पर खुदा हुआ लेख)
58.example: The silver coin carried an inscription bearing the name of Queen Begum Nur Jahan.

58.english_meaning: An official royal order or decree issued by a sovereign in Islamic or Mughal context.
58.example: The adjoining document in the textbook is an official farman issued by Nur Jahan.

58.english_meaning: Of such excellence, grandeur, or beauty as to inspire great admiration.
58.example: The royal seal spoke of the command of her most sublime and elevated majesty.

58.english_meaning: Raised to a higher status, position, or rank.
58.example: She held an elevated position of power and authority within the imperial court.

58.english_meaning: Very bright, shining, or impressively clever and successful.
58.example: Under the light of Shah Jahangir, she became as brilliant as the moon.

58.english_meaning: A person who attends a royal court as an adviser or companion to the monarch.
58.hindi_meaning: दरबारी (राजा के दरबार का सदस्य या सलाहकार)
58.example: Abul Fazl was one of the closest friends and trusted courtiers of Emperor Akbar.

58.english_meaning: The period during which a sovereign rules.
58.example: Abul Fazl wrote a detailed three-volume history documenting Akbar's reign.

58.english_meaning: A person from whom one is descended, typically one more remote than a grandparent.
58.example: The first volume of Akbar Nama dealt with the ancestry and lineage of Akbar.

58.english_meaning: The process or activity of running a business, organization, or government.
58.example: The Ain-i Akbari provides extensive details regarding the empire's administration.

58.english_meaning: Income, especially of a company or organization and of a government through taxation.
58.example: The text discusses the revenues collected from land and agriculture during the Mughal era.

58.english_meaning: The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
58.example: The book provides rich insights into the traditions and culture of the people of India.

58.english_meaning: Relating to the use of statistics (numerical data and facts).
58.example: The Ain-i Akbari contains rich statistical details on agricultural yields and prices.

58.english_meaning: Showing a great deal of variety; very different.
58.example: The document records statistical details about diverse subjects like crops, wages, and prices.

59.english_meaning: A policy of 'universal peace' introduced by Emperor Akbar, promoting religious tolerance and harmony among different faiths.
59.hindi_meaning: सार्वभौमिक शांति या 'कुल शांति', अकबर की धार्मिक सहिष्णुता की नीति।
59.example: Akbar's policy of sulh-i kul ensured that people of all religions could live and worship freely in the empire.

59.english_meaning: Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
59.example: The ruler showed great compassion toward the poor and marginalized people in his kingdom.

59.english_meaning: A particular set of religious beliefs or faiths.
59.example: People belonging to various creeds and backgrounds gathered peacefully in the empire.

59.english_meaning: Sovereignty or control; the territory controlled by a ruler or government.
59.example: The emperor expanded his dominions across the subcontinent.

59.english_meaning: In this historical context, people who profess or practice a particular religion or belief.
59.hindi_meaning: अनुयायी या किसी धर्म/मत को मानने वाले।
59.example: Professors of opposite religions lived together in harmony under the new policy.

59.english_meaning: Unwillingness to accept views, beliefs, or behavior that differ from one's own.
59.example: The government strictly ensured that the road to religious intolerance was closed.

59.english_meaning: In every case or on every occasion; invariably.
59.example: He consistently followed the principle of non-violence in his administration.

59.english_meaning: Relating to the running of a business, organization, or nation.
59.example: The administrative efficiency of the Mughal Empire helped in maintaining internal peace.

59.english_meaning: The state of being prosperous, successful, or wealthy.
59.example: Trade and agriculture brought great economic prosperity to the region.
Foreign visitors were appalled at the extreme poverty existing alongside great wealth.
The royal court was known for its unmatched opulence and grandeur.

59.english_meaning: Differences in size, degree, circumstances, or wealth; lack of equality.
59.example: The glaring economic inequalities between the rich nobles and poor peasants were evident.

59.english_meaning: Roughly calculated or judged in value, number, or quantity.
59.example: The estimated revenue of the empire was calculated at the beginning of the financial year.

59.english_meaning: Income, especially when of a company or organization and of a substantial nature (or taxes collected by the state).
59.hindi_meaning: राजस्व या सरकारी आय (कर आदि से प्राप्त धन)।
59.example: Land revenue was the primary source of income for the Mughal state.

59.english_meaning: Soldiers in a cavalry unit or armed troopers.
59.example: The nobles maintained a large number of troopers for military service.

59.english_meaning: A worker in a skilled trade, especially one that involves making things by hand.
59.example: Potters, weavers, and metalworkers are examples of skilled artisans.

59.english_meaning: People who directly produce raw goods, such as farmers, peasants, and primary agricultural workers.
59.hindi_meaning: प्राथमिक उत्पादक (जैसे किसान और खेतीहार मजदूर)।
59.example: Primary producers bore the heaviest burden of revenue collection in the empire.

59.english_meaning: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be used to function effectively.
59.example: The farmers lacked enough resources to purchase better seeds and tools.

60.english_meaning: The state or quality of producing something, especially in large quantities.
60.example: New agricultural techniques were introduced to increase productivity on the farms.

60.english_meaning: The class of small farmers and farm laborers of low social status.
60.example: The wealthier peasantry played a significant role in the rural economy.

60.english_meaning: A select group that is superior in terms of ability or qualities to the rest of a group or society.
60.example: The Mughal elite commanded enormous wealth and resources in the empire.

60.english_meaning: To have control over something, or to be in a position to demand something.
60.example: The nobles commanded vast estates and numerous troops.

60.english_meaning: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
60.example: As the authority of the Mughal emperor declined, regional powers emerged.

60.english_meaning: To become smaller, fewer, or worse; to decrease in power or strength.
60.example: The political influence of the central court slowly declined during the late seventeenth century.

60.english_meaning: To be the parts or elements of something, or to establish/form something.
60.example: They constituted new dynasties in various regions of the empire.

60.english_meaning: A line of hereditary rulers of a country.
60.example: Several new dynasties were established in the provinces of Hyderabad and Awadh.

60.english_meaning: A principal administrative division of certain countries or empires.
60.example: The governor held command over important provinces like Hyderabad and Awadh.

60.english_meaning: To accept and acknowledge the validity or authority of someone.
60.example: The regional rulers continued to recognise the Mughal emperor in Delhi as their master.

60.english_meaning: To make something stronger or more secure; to combine into a single more effective unit.
60.example: By the eighteenth century, the provinces had consolidated their independent political identities.

60.english_meaning: The fact of being who or what a person or nation is.
